name: Combining Financial and Non-Financial Data
title: Combining Financial and Non-Financial Data
answer: Combining financial and non-financial data means bringing together figures from the general ledger, such as spend, revenue and cost, with measures that never appear in it, such as emissions, energy use, headcount, water draw or supplier ratings. In sustainability and carbon accounting the aim is usually to attach a carbon or other impact figure to a monetary one, so that a cost line and its associated emissions can be read side by side. The work sits between the finance function and the sustainability team, and it draws on procurement records, utility bills, meter data, travel systems and supplier questionnaires as well as the accounting system itself.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Combining financial and non-financial data means bringing together figures from the general ledger, such as spend, revenue and cost, with measures that never appear in it, such as emissions, energy use, headcount, water draw or supplier ratings. In sustainability and carbon accounting the aim is usually to attach a carbon or other impact figure to a monetary one, so that a cost line and its associated emissions can be read side by side. The work sits between the finance function and the sustainability team, and it draws on procurement records, utility bills, meter data, travel systems and supplier questionnaires as well as the accounting system itself.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The base layer is the ERP and the chart of accounts, because most non-financial data has to be tied back to an entity, a cost centre or a purchase order before it can be combined with anything financial. Alongside that sit source systems for activity data, meter and utility feeds, fleet and travel records, and supplier disclosure platforms, plus a data warehouse or lakehouse where the two streams are staged. Matching keys, unit tables and emission factor libraries do much of the real work, and spreadsheets remain common at the edges even where a dedicated platform is in place.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The practical method is to define a common key, usually supplier, site, cost centre or purchase order, then map each non-financial record to a financial one and reconcile the totals. Activity data is multiplied by an emission factor to give a carbon figure, which is then allocated across the same periods and boundaries the finance team uses. Estimation fills gaps where primary data is missing, and spend-based methods are common as a starting point before supplier-specific data replaces them. Machine learning tends to appear in classification, anomaly detection and document extraction, for example reading utility bills or supplier certificates, rather than in the calculation itself.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risks are boundary mismatch, double counting, estimated data presented as measured, and restatements when factors or methods change. Controls therefore cover who owns each figure, how estimates are flagged, how units and factors are versioned, and how a number can be traced back to its source document. Assurance providers ask for that trail, and the finance team's existing materiality and sign-off habits usually shape it. This is a description of common practice, not legal or accounting advice, and reporting obligations vary by jurisdiction and framework.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward tighter coupling between the two datasets, with carbon figures carried at transaction level rather than assembled once a year. Regulatory reporting is pulling non-financial disclosure closer to financial reporting discipline, and assurance expectations are rising with it. Better supplier-specific data and wider use of extraction and matching tools should reduce reliance on spend-based estimates over time. The open questions are comparability across frameworks and how quickly the underlying data quality can catch up with the reporting ambition.
